passage: In the Kowalski laboratory, researchers measured dehydrogenase activity in a liver homogenate by following production of NADH, which absorbs light at 340 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 6,220 M⁻¹cm⁻¹, whereas NAD⁺ does not absorb appreciably at this wavelength. The homogenate was diluted 50-fold in assay buffer before use, and 1 mL reactions in a 1 cm cuvette contained saturating substrate and NAD⁺ at 25 °C. Absorbance at 340 nm was recorded every minute. A blank containing all components except substrate was run in parallel to correct for non-enzymatic changes. The initial linear region of the progress curve was used to calculate velocity. The researchers wished to report the activity of the undiluted homogenate and to compare it with a published value from a different laboratory. The spectrophotometer was zeroed against buffer, and all readings fell within the instrument's linear range. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What is the change in A340 of the sample between 0 and 2 minutes, according to Table 1?
questions.trap: Subtracting the 0 min reading from the 3 min reading (0.423 - 0.05 = 0.373) instead of the 2 min reading.

questions.stem: Why is a blank lacking substrate included?

options.A: To ensure the enzyme is saturated
options.B: To increase the extinction coefficient of NADH
options.C: To detect absorbance changes that occur without the enzyme-catalyzed reaction

questions.explanation: The blank accounts for background drift (e.g., contaminating reductants, instrument drift) independent of the reaction under study.
questions.trap: Believing the blank saturates the enzyme or raises the signal, when its purpose is to reveal non-enzymatic absorbance change.

questions.stem: Using Beer–Lambert, what is the initial rate of NADH formation in the cuvette (µM/min), and what activity does the undiluted homogenate have (µM/min)?

options.A: 20 µM/min in the cuvette; 20 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.B: 0.02 µM/min in the cuvette; 1 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.C: 1000 µM/min in the cuvette; 50000 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate
options.D: 20 µM/min in the cuvette; 1000 µM/min in the undiluted homogenate

questions.explanation: Rate = (ΔA/min)/(ε·l) = 0.1244/6220 = 20 µM/min in the cuvette. Multiply by the 50-fold dilution to get 1000 µM/min for the undiluted homogenate.
questions.trap: Forgetting the 50-fold dilution and reporting the cuvette rate of 20 µM/min as the activity of the undiluted homogenate.

questions.stem: Which statement about this assay is INCORRECT?

options.A: NADH absorbs at 340 nm while NAD⁺ does not
options.B: Substrate must be saturating for the rate to approximate Vmax
options.C: Both NAD⁺ and NADH absorb strongly at 340 nm, so the signal reflects total coenzyme
options.D: The initial linear portion of the curve gives the most reliable velocity

questions.explanation: Only the reduced coenzyme absorbs at 340 nm; that selective absorbance makes the assay possible.
questions.trap: Believing NAD⁺ also absorbs strongly at 340 nm so the signal tracks total coenzyme; only NADH absorbs there, which makes the assay work.

questions.stem: Which type of assay couples an enzyme of interest to NADH oxidation so that its activity can be monitored at 340 nm?

options.A: A radioactive assay using ³²P-labeled ATP
options.B: A gel assay using SDS-PAGE mobility
options.C: A coupled assay using lactate dehydrogenase to reduce pyruvate formed by pyruvate kinase
options.D: An immunoassay using antibodies against the enzyme

questions.explanation: Pyruvate kinase produces pyruvate; LDH then oxidizes NADH to NAD⁺, causing a decrease in A340 proportional to pyruvate kinase activity.
questions.trap: Choosing a radioactive, gel or antibody assay, none of which links enzyme activity to NADH absorbance at 340 nm.
